mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Direct Corporate Shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the certified copy, then either obtain a Hague Apostille from the designated authority of the issuing country if it is an Apostille Convention member, or undergo Consular Legalization at the Republic of Korea Embassy or Consulate having jurisdiction if the issuing country is not a member; the two paths are parallel and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing from the Shareholder's Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Same competent company registry as the certificate of incorporation, acting as the official registrar
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by the issuing registry; Hague Apostille for Apostille Convention jurisdictions, or Consular Legalization at the Korean diplomatic post for non-member jurisdictions; choose only the path applicable to the document origin.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution Authorizing Incorporation and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or board of directors of the ultimate parent shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the signatures on the resolution and power of attorney; for apostille countries attach a Hague Apostille, for non-apostille countries attach consular legalization by the Korean Consulate; never apply both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Certified copy of the ultimate shareholder's constitutional documents)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ultimate shareholder company, confirmed by the company secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized true copy; if issued in an Apostille state, legalize solely via Hague Apostille; if issued in a non-member state, legalize solely via Consular Legalization at the relevant Korean embassy or consulate.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship bank of the corporate shareholder in its country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the bank's signatory official; apostille for Hague-member issuing country or consular legalization for non-member issuing country, used as a standalone standard.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Ultimate Beneficial Owner Declaration and Source of Wealth Questionnaire
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each ultimate beneficial owner (natural person) and the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execute before a notary public; attach Hague Apostille if the executing state is an Apostille member, or Consular Legalization if the executing state is not a member. Both methods are mutually exclusive and no combination is permitted.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before filing, counsel must run automated and human-enhanced screening across all UBOs, directors, authorized signatories, and commercial counterparties against OFAC SDN and consolidated lists, UN Security Council Resolution 1267/1988/2231 consolidated sanctions list, EU consolidated financial sanctions database, Korean Financial Services Commission and KoFIU sanctions/travel-ban notices, and domestic criminal-wanted databases. Politically exposed persons (PEPs), including heads of state, ministers, senior judicial and military officials, and their immediate family and close associates, trigger mandatory enhanced due diligence, requiring documented source of wealth and source of funds, independent public-source negative news investigation, senior management approval, ongoing transaction monitoring, and record retention for at least five years after termination of the business relationship. No share capital may be introduced or funds disbursed until all screening is cleared and the compliance file is signed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Electronic Registration Office (I-SAR) at https://www.iros.go.kr and the National Tax Service Bizinfo portal at https://www.bizinfo.go.kr for business-name and taxpayer-status conflict screening.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Article 19 of the Korean Commercial Act, the corporate name must be written in Hangul; a foreign-language name may be used in parallel only after the Hangul name and, if necessary, must be phonetically transliterated into Hangul. The registry applies a four-tier naming convention: (1) a distinctive core word, (2) a business-description term reflecting ISIC 6201 and AI/LLM API activity, (3) a legal form indicator such as Chusik Hoesa or Corporation, and (4) an optional English parallel name. The name must not be identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered name in a related business class and must be visually and phonetically distinguishable.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 days of receiving a rejection, counsel must file a written objection with the chief registry judge of the district court that supervises the intended registered office, stating the legal grounds for distinctiveness and attaching corrected alternative names. If the registry judge upholds the rejection, a petition for adjudication may be filed to the appellate court under the Commercial Registration Act, and the company may simultaneously re-file with a revised name. Parallel submission of two to three alternative names is mandatory, and the administrative appeal must be exhausted before executing any share subscription agreement.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Korean commercial registration requires a definite street address and the articles of association must state the city, county or district of the head office; a commercial mailbox alone is not a registrable address for a Chusik Hoesa. For this AI/LLM API token business, the National Tax Service requires a physical place of business for VAT and corporate income tax filings and will scrutinize addresses that appear to be mail-forwarding only. Most Korean banks reject pure virtual offices for corporate account opening, especially for foreign-owned entities, and require a formal lease, utility bill, signage, or an in-person branch visit. A compliant serviced office or shared office with a dedicated lease, floor plan and company name plate is permissible and operational; a standalone virtual mailbox is not recommended and will likely be refused.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (a) lease or service office agreement with floor plan; (b) company name plate attached to the registered office; (c) staff or authorized representative available during business hours; (d) utility or facility bills in the company name; (e) contemporaneous access logs and visitor register. Unannounced inspection likelihood: 5-8% for a one-director, fully digital AI platform with no physical inventory; 12-20% if the registered office is a virtual-office address shared by more than five unrelated companies or lacks physical signage; 25-35% where payroll or subcontractor filings indicate employees in Korea but no active work site. Counsel should retain remote monitoring records and ensure the office manager is trained to receive Supreme Court Registry or National Tax Service inspectors on 24-hour notice.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Korean Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as fully amended), principally Articles 288 through 318 (formation, shares, capital and registration of a stock company; Title III, Chapter II), together with the Registration of Real Estate and Corporations Act (Act No. 5364, as amended) and the Commercial Act Enforcement Decree, governing the incorporation registration of a Chusik Hoesa.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Korea Supreme Court (Registration Bureau) and the District Court Registration Division having territorial jurisdiction over the company's registered office; electronic submissions are made through Korea Internet Court Registration Service (KICS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Stock Company (corporate registration application) under Article 301 of the Korean Commercial Act and Article 25 of the Registration of Real Estate and Corporations Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None (no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a non-regulated Chusik Hoesa). The entire par or issue price of each subscribed share must be fully paid before incorporation; the subscribed proceeds must be deposited into a blocked pre-incorporation bank account in the name of a promoter or agent in a Korean bank and may not be withdrawn until the corporate registration is completed. For this AI/LLM API platform, the articles will provide authorized capital of KRW 100,000,000 and initial fully paid paid-in capital of KRW 10,000,000, all subscribed and deposited before registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FOR THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [LEGAL NAME] CHUSIK HOESA, a corporation to be organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, adopted by unanimous written consent or at a duly convened meeting at the registered office on ________.

WHEREAS the founding shareholders have subscribed to the entire initial share capital and have caused the full subscription price to be deposited and held in the blocked account designated by the promoters; and

WHEREAS the election of the initial directors and the adoption of the registered office must be formalized prior to the registration of incorporation;

NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED as follows:

1. SHARE CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION. The directors ratify the subscription list and the issuance of ________ fully paid registered ordinary shares of par value ________ Korean won per share, for an aggregate paid-in capital of ________ Korean won. The Board confirms that the certificate of capital payment issued by [Bank] evidencing blocked receipt of the full subscription proceeds is true and correct. Upon completion of incorporation registration, this amount shall constitute the company's paid-in capital and the account shall be converted to the company's operating account.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office and principal place of business of the company is adopted and fixed at [full address], Republic of Korea. The representative director is authorized to execute and deliver the office lease, register the address with the competent District Court Registration Division, and notify the National Tax Service and all relevant authorities.

3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The representative director is hereby vested with full authority to open, operate, close and designate one or more bank accounts in the company's name, to sign cheques and wire-transfer instructions, to designate Stripe as a payment processor and, after legal and AML/KYC review, USDC or cryptocurrency settlement processors as payment rails, and to appoint any commercial bank, foreign exchange bank or payment institution necessary for the company's business.

4. STATUTORY OFFICERS. ________ is appointed representative director. ________ is appointed director. If required by the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, ________ is appointed statutory auditor. Each officer's consent to act has been obtained and shall be filed with the registration application.

5. GOVERNANCE FILINGS. The directors adopt the corporate seal, approve the application for incorporation registration, authorize payment of all official fees and registration taxes, and engage external counsel and corporate service providers to attend to the filing.

6. EFFECTIVENESS. This resolution is valid effective immediately and shall remain in force until lawfully revoked. Any officer is authorized to execute all documents, checks, declarations and certifications necessary to carry out the foregoing.

PASSED UNANIMOUSLY ON ________. CHAIRPERSON ________, DIRECTORS ________.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Internet Court Registration Service (KICS) and the local District Court Registration Division for the intended registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before drafting the constitutive documents, perform a mandatory legal capacity and name availability review. Search the national corporate registry through KICS using the proposed Korean name and its English equivalent to ensure that no registered company has an identical or confusingly similar name. Confirm that the promoters are not disqualified persons under the Korean Commercial Act and that the proposed registered office lies within a single District Court registration district. Prepare the shareholder subscription schedule showing each founding shareholder, nationality, Korean registration number if applicable, subscribed shares and contribution amount. If names differ in Korean and English, align the English name with the Korean registered form. The authority will issue an electronic confirmation of name availability or a rejection with reasons, enabling the next step to proceed without correction disputes.
required_dossiers: Proposed Korean corporate name and English name
Identification and nationality details of each promoter
Proposed registered office address and district
Share subscription schedule
Promoters' consent forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name conflict or supplemental order is issued, correct the name or add a distinguishing regional identifier and re-file through KICS; the turnaround recommences. If the registry requests promoter eligibility documents, submit notarized identity papers within two business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public authorized by the Ministry of Justice in the venue of the promoters or their agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation under Articles 289 and 292 of the Korean Commercial Act and submit them to a notary for certification. The instrument must state the corporate purpose, corporate name, registered office, total authorized shares, par value, classes of shares, initial paid-in capital, director and statutory auditor provisions, notice period, publication method if any, financial year end, and liquidation provisions. Each promoter or a proper agent must appear before the notary, confirm the articles, and execute them with a corporate seal or personal sign. The notary will verify the promoters' identities and legal capacity, read the instrument, and certify a notarial certificate attached to the articles. After notarization, no material change may be made without a new notarial act. The notarized articles are the key instrument for share subscription and registration.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Identity documents and seal certificates of all promoters
Power of attorney if an agent appears
Notarization fee payment confirmation
Written statement of promoters' personal details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses certification due to illegality or missing clauses, revise the articles, obtain unanimous promoter consent, and re-present. If an unnotarized page is detected, cure by notarizing the corrected page or re-notarizing the entire set before the next step.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription, Deposit and Blocked Account Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank duly established in Korea, acting as depository bank for the pre-incorporation capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a pre-incorporation deposit account in the name of the promoter or an expressly authorized agent. Each subscriber must execute a share subscription application and pay the full issue price in Korean won for all subscribed shares. For contributions in kind, obtain a court-appointed inspector's valuation report and attach it to the subscription record. The depository bank will issue a certificate of capital payment or deposit receipt, which is required for the inaugural general meeting and the registration application. The account remains blocked until legal personality is obtained; no withdrawal is permitted before the registration. The depository institution must be named in the application and the amount deposited must correspond exactly to the initial paid-in capital in the articles. Any underpayment invalidates the accompanying share subscriptions.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Share subscription applications of each subscriber
Promoters' identity certificates
Bank deposit application and AML/KYC forms
In-kind property valuation report (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the deposit instruction for KYC/AML insufficiency, supply corrected source-of-funds statements and re-file within the same banking day. If the deposit certificate states a lower amount, pay the deficiency and obtain a supplementary certificate before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inaugural General Meeting and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate governance body convened by promoters; executed at the registered office or through lawful electronic means
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the inaugural general meeting of all subscribers after the deposit certificate is issued. The meeting must elect the first directors and, if required by law or the articles, a statutory auditor. The elected directors must consent to their appointment. Immediately after election, the directors hold the first board meeting and pass the formal first board resolution ratifying share capital subscription, adopting the registered office, appointing the representative director, authorizing bank account opening and settlement rails, and approving the corporate registration filing. The minutes of both meetings must record the attendance list, quorum, voting results, and each officer's acceptance. Minutes must be signed by the chairperson and the directors, and notarized if the registry of the competent district requires it. These minutes are necessary to evidence officer authority at registration.
required_dossiers: Convening notice and attendance list
Minutes of the inaugural general meeting
Minutes of the first board of directors meeting
Consent forms of directors, representative director and statutory auditor
Certificate of capital payment from the depository bank
Original notarized Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a convening defect is raised, cure by obtaining unanimous written consent of all subscribers or by holding a second meeting with proper notice. If a director fails to consent, replace the officer and pass a new board resolution before the registration filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court Registration of Incorporation and Corporate Seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Registration Division within the jurisdiction of the registered office; electronically via KICS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Application for Registration of Establishment of a Stock Company with the competent District Court Registration Division. Attach the notarized articles, certificate of capital payment, minute books, directors' consent, seal certificate of the representative director, and payment receipt for registration tax and local education surtax. The court registrar will review the lawfulness of the incorporation and the correctness of the register. Upon approval, the registry assigns a corporate registration number, records the directors and representative director, and returns the sealed certificate of corporate registration and an authentication of the corporate register. The corporate legal personality is completed on this filing date. Thereafter, obtain the corporate seal certificate and the company's registration certificate from the registry and use them for tax and banking steps.
required_dossiers: Corporate registration application form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank certificate of capital payment
Inaugural general meeting minutes and first board resolution
Consent to office by directors and statutory auditor
Power of attorney for filing agent
Certificate of payment of registration tax and education surtax
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a supplementary order, submit the requested correction within two weeks; otherwise the filing may be invalidated. If the registry rejects registration, refile promptly with corrected instruments, or apply for rectification under the Registration of Real Estate and Corporations Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Service Business Registration and Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) district tax office for business and VAT registration; depository bank for account conversion
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After corporation registration, file the application for business registration with the NTS district tax office within one month. Attach the certificate of corporate registration, corporate seal certificate, articles of incorporation, registered office lease, and representative director's identification. The NTS will issue the business registration certificate and assign the taxpayer identification number, VAT registration, and corporate income tax file. Present the NTS certificate and the court registration documents to the depository bank to convert the blocked pre-incorporation account into the company's operating account in the corporate name. The representative director must execute the bank's corporate account application and KYC declaration. This completes the statutory formation cycle and enables obtaining payment rail credentials and executing commercial contracts.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate registration from the court registry
Corporate seal certificate
Application for business registration (NTS form)
Registered office lease agreement
Articles of Incorporation
Representative director's identification and personal seal certificate
Corporate bank account opening application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If NTS requests further proof of address, submit a revised lease or utility invoice within 14 days. If the bank refuses the account conversion based on unresolved beneficial ownership filings, provide corrective source-of-funds and ultimate beneficial owner declarations and resubmit the KYC package the same day.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the entity is a pure digital generative AI and LLM inference API platform under ISIC 6201 with no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, warehouse, or other physical industrial operation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating permit is required for software and AI API services in Korea. Any future office-based occupational clearances remain governed by the Occupational Safety and Health Act, but no industrial manufacturing licence is triggered.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - no ministry of environment assessment is triggered for a non-physical software activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA Report and Environmental Registration because the operation is office-based digital service with no construction or discharge site.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no industrial wastewater, VOCs, hazardous waste storage, or point-source emissions. If the company later builds a data center, laboratory or warehouse, the environmental impact assessment must be re-opened under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act and Wastes Control Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no Civil Defense fire permit, structural load inspection, or hazardous-process workplace certification is required for an AI API platform. Only general workplace safety obligations under the Occupational Safety and Health Act apply to the office premises, including fire extinguishers, evacuation routes and electrical safety inspections.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS); electronic tax portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Korean-resident Chusik Hoesa: after completing incorporation registration with the Korean commercial registry, the entity must apply for a Business Registration Certificate under the Value-Added Tax Act at the competent District Tax Office of the NTS for its principal domestic place of business, submitting articles of incorporation, incorporation registration certificate, place-of-business lease evidence, and director identification documents; the NTS issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number, which serves as the corporate TIN and VAT ID, and the entity must then enroll in HomeTax for VAT returns, electronic tax invoices, and withholding reporting. For a foreign non-resident entity with no Korean place of business that supplies electronic services to Korean consumers: (1) the foreign entity must appoint a Korean tax representative under the Framework Act on National Taxes; (2) the tax representative must file a foreign business operator VAT registration application with the District Tax Office designated by the NTS for foreign electronic service suppliers, attaching the foreign entity's certificate of incorporation, evidence of the electronic service offering, and a signed power of attorney in favor of the tax representative; (3) upon approval, the NTS issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number for VAT purposes; (4) the foreign entity uses this number to file quarterly VAT returns through HomeTax and to issue electronic tax invoices where B2B supply occurs; (5) any change in the tax representative, foreign address, or electronic service platform must be reported to the NTS within the statutory amendment period. For non-resident B2B electronic service suppliers, the Korean recipient may instead apply reverse-charge VAT where no registration is required, but B2C electronic services to Korean individuals require the foreign operator registration path described above.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not operate check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch entity classification elections; a Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily taxed at the entity level as a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No KRW turnover threshold. Every business operator, including a Chusik Hoesa, must register for VAT upon commencement of business. A foreign non-resident electronic service supplier making B2C supplies to Korean consumers must register from the first taxable supply; there is no de minimis turnover threshold for that registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory certified electronic tax invoices must be issued through HomeTax or an NTS-approved electronic tax invoice service provider (ASP); e-invoice data is transmitted to the NTS electronically in near real time upon issuance, and the invoice must be issued within the statutory issuance period under Article 32 of the Value-Added Tax Act. Input VAT deduction generally requires the purchaser to hold and report a valid electronic tax invoice. The Electronic Cash Receipt system is additionally mandatory for qualifying B2C transactions paid by card or cash. There is no separate fiscal stamp; anti-fraud controls rely on real-time e-invoice transmission, NTS invoice matching, and administrative penalties for late, incorrect, or omitted electronic tax invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Value-Added Tax Act and its Enforcement Decree, 0% VAT applies to exported goods and to services supplied to foreign non-residents where the service is considered consumed outside Korea and the consideration is derived from foreign exchange earnings. For the AI/LLM API platform, zero-rating is available for: (i) B2B subscription and token-based API usage fees charged to foreign business customers under a written contract where the recipient has no Korean establishment and the service is delivered abroad; (ii) B2C API/token purchases by foreign consumers where the platform can evidence the customer's foreign residency and overseas consumption of the service; and (iii) exported digital content and software services supplied to overseas users. The exporter must maintain the statutory substantiation file proving the foreign customer, foreign currency receipt, and actual delivery/output outside Korea. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated exports may be claimed as a refund on the quarterly VAT return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service export declaration confirmation (export declaration) for physical goods only; not applicable to pure AI/LLM API exports
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for physical goods; for digital services, the service delivery log and API usage/token consumption report serve as delivery evidence
Commercial invoice or electronic tax invoice stating the foreign customer and zero-rated nature of the supply
Written service agreement/API subscription contract with the foreign customer confirming the overseas place of supply
Foreign Exchange Acquisition Certificate or inward remittance evidence issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank proving repatriation of the export proceeds
Foreign customer's overseas business registration certificate or other foreign residency/status evidence for B2B and B2C services respectively
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the NTS determines that export zero-rating is not substantiated, the supply will be reclassified as domestic taxable, 10% VAT will be assessed on the gross supply, and the input VAT previously credited or refunded against zero-rated exports will be clawed back with interest. Administrative penalties for false tax invoices, false export declarations, or understated VAT bases will be imposed under the Value-Added Tax Act, and intentional or grossly negligent evasion may trigger criminal sanctions under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. Repeat violations can also result in increased audit frequency, stricter documentary requirements, and cancellation of the exporter's zero-rating entitlement.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central bank, with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) responsible for exchange control policy and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA) providing the enforcement framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea exercises a legally regulated but operationally efficient exchange control system. Current account transactions such as software export revenue, technical service fees, royalty receipts, and ordinary operating expenses are quasi-automatically convertible for Korean legal entities through banks that are designated foreign exchange banks. Payment instructions require a stated purpose, the underlying invoice or contract, and reasonable source-of-funds or destination support, but no pre-approval is required for most bona fide service flows. Capital account transactions are substantially more restricted: a non-resident shareholder contributing equity into a Chusik Hoesa must complete foreign direct investment reporting through a designated foreign exchange bank, obtain the FDI registration confirmation, and evidence the inbound SWIFT remittance. The Korean won is not a fully freely convertible currency for speculation or pure capital account transfers. Profit remittance by dividend or liquidation distribution is permitted as a current account remittance only after the bank reviews audited financial statements, withholding tax payment receipts, and the original FDI registration record. Export proceeds are not subject to compulsory conversion into KRW; the entity may retain hard currency in foreign-currency deposit accounts. The principal compliance friction arises from ensuring that every inward and outward remittance is mapped to an approved purpose code and supported by documentation consistent with the international operation and the AI LLM API revenue model.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and Enforcement Decree, exporters of goods or digital services, including AI/LLM API services, must procure the export proceeds within six months from the date of export declaration or service completion. There is no mandatory surrender ratio requiring conversion of earned hard currency into KRW; proceeds may be withheld in foreign currency accounts held at a domestic designated foreign exchange bank. If the commercial settlement terms require a longer collection period, the exporter must submit an extension request to its designated foreign exchange bank before the original deadline expires, accompanied by the underlying master service agreement, billing milestone schedule, and a foreign receivable aging certificate.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary treasury rail; medium only as an ancillary foreign-currency receivable collector. Foreign fintech EMIs such as Airwallex, Currenxie, Wise Business, or Stripe Treasury do not possess a Korean banking license under the Banking Act and cannot issue KRW current accounts or access the Korean won clearing system. Using an EMI as the principal bank account for a Korean corporation would violate the Electronic Financial Transactions Act because the EMI is not an authorized domestic financial institution. Such EMIs may be used for selective offshore foreign-currency deposit and cross-border payout niche collections, but funds managed through an EMI must eventually be repatriated to a designated Korean bank via a documented SWIFT transfer and reported under the applicable FETA purpose code. Korean underwriting banks generally do not accept EMI transaction statements as conclusive evidence of export proceeds or paid-in capital; therefore, the Chusik Hoesa must maintain its statutory treasury account at a domestic Tier-1 commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors who are foreign residents are generally required to appear physically at the designated foreign exchange bank for the corporate account opening interview. Some banks permit remote opening or consular proxy opening when a notarized power of attorney is apostilled under the Hague Convention, translated into Korean and affirmed by a certified translator, and accompanied by passport copies and criminal record background statements. However, the bank mandate committee retains discretionary risk-based authority to demand an in-branch appearance from the ultimate beneficial owner before releasing full foreign currency capacities. Remote video KYC alone is not a standard route for a non-resident-owned Korean Chusik Hoesa in the current supervisory environment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ambiguous beneficial ownership chain where a non-resident natural person indirectly controls the Korean Chusik Hoesa through an overseas holding company, creating a nominee shareholder red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified share register and certificate of good standing for the overseas holding company; apostilled passport and proof of residential address for every natural person above the 25% threshold; corporate organizational chart with exact ownership percentages; notarized board resolution resolving to open the account; signed non-nominee declaration and UBO statement; certified translation of all corporate records into Korean.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export of intangible AI/LLM API services with no customs declaration, shipping documents, or logistics trail to validate the trade purpose and defend against cross-border invoice fraud.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial master service agreements with named enterprise clients; detailed itemized invoice ledger showing token volume, API pricing, service dates and settlement ids; proof of domain hosting and production service logs; ISO 27001 and SOC 2 attestation reports; client payment confirmation emails; a bank-side demonstration of the technical platform through a live API sandbox; software export certificate or intangible asset export report if required by the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The stated target payment rails include USDC/cryptocurrency settlement, which may trigger AML concerns relating to unhosted wallets, sanctions evasion, or unlicensed virtual asset activity in Korea.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A formal company treasury policy declaring that cryptocurrency is received only through qualified foreign virtual asset service providers; wallet addresses and chain analytics reports showing source-of-funds traceability; copies of the foreign VASP license verification; executive certification that USDC is immediately converted into fiat through a regulated venue and that inward remittance is separately documented; Korean legal opinion on the Travelex rules under the Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information Act; a commitment to terminate crypto settlement if the designated bank objects.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital injection from a non-resident parent into a newly formed low-minimum-capital Korean tech entity, raising concern over cross-border money brokerage, foreign exchange evasion, or thin capitalization abuse.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FDI reporting acknowledgment issued by the designated foreign exchange bank; the bank's MT103 telex with the specific FDI purpose code; a notarized share subscription agreement; board minutes approving the issuance of shares; bank-certified securities filtering and inward remittance certificate; a source-of-funds statement from the investing shareholder; tax identification number of the investor; audited or attorney-reviewed financial statements explaining the deployment of the attracted capital in the AI/LLM project; a mutual business plan aligned with the ISIC 6201 scope.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound foreign direct investment should be routed exclusively through the SWIFT MT103 protocol from the foreign investor's bank directly to the Chusik Hoesa's designated foreign exchange bank in Korea. The SWIFT instruction must include the purpose code specified for foreign direct investment and the beneficiary account in the name of the Chusik Hoesa. The designated bank will require an FDI report through the Foreign Exchange Information System, issue a paid-in capital receipt, and provide the certificate of inward remittance and FDI registration confirmation. This capital receipt is then submitted to the Korean commercial registry office as part of the capital verification process. The treasury must not use cryptocurrency rails or fintech EMIs for the equity injection because the capital verification file will be rejected during the statutory corporate registration process.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For a Korean generative AI and LLM API platform, outbound trade disbursements will primarily settle software royalties, cloud infrastructure fees, independent contractor billing, and dividend distributions. The most efficient rail is SWIFT MT103 for recurring service payments and intercompany fees, supported by the upstream contract, VAT invoice, and withholding tax receipt. Commercial documentary Letters of Credit are appropriate when the treasury procures physical GPU servers or networked hardware from foreign suppliers; Documentary Collections provide a lower-cost compromise for time-tested supply agreements. All outbound wire instructions require a compliant purpose code, complete tax compliance, and sufficient proof of the underlying commercial transaction, and the bank may block remittances if the recipient jurisdiction appears on the FIU list or the KYC file is stale.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary General Meeting of Shareholders and approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the Chusik Hoesa; corporate resolution recorded in the official Minute Book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of each financial year; for a December 31 fiscal year, on or before March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A resolution adopted in violation of the Korean Commercial Act is voidable; directors may be subject to administrative fines of up to KRW 5,000,000; persistent failure to convene an ordinary general meeting and maintain statutory books can lead to judicial dissolution proceedings under Commercial Act Article 176, but there is no automatic administrative registry strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via the HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the financial year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year, by March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file attracts an additional tax equal to 20 percent of the unpaid corporate income tax; under-reporting triggers a 10 percent additional tax; late-payment additional tax accrues on the outstanding amount; chronic non-payment permits tax seizure, cancellation of business registration, and compulsory collection under the National Tax Collection Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Local Income Tax return and settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government authority of the head-office jurisdiction, filed through the local tax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the financial year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year, by March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An unfiled local income tax return carries a 20 percent additional tax on the unpaid amount; under-reporting carries a 10 percent additional tax; daily late-payment surcharges and local tax seizure or compulsory enforcement follow persistent default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Certified external audit report filing (conditionally mandatory if the statutory audit threshold is exceeded)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Independent licensed certified public accountant, the National Tax Service, and for publicly disclosing companies the Financial Supervisory Service electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Auditor appointment must be completed before the statutory audit period; audited financial statements must accompany the annual tax filing; for a December 31 fiscal year, the audit report is due on or before March 31 of the following year unless a lawful extension applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A company required to be externally audited that fails to appoint an auditor or file audited financial statements faces sanctions under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, including fines and invalidation of tax-filing reliance on the unaudited statements; the false or omitted audit report may also disqualify the company from certain regulatory privileges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-invested enterprise material change report and annual foreign investment maintenance report (conditional on non-resident or foreign direct investment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) or the reporting foreign exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any shareholding transfer or capital alteration affecting the foreign investment particulars must be reported within 30 days of the transaction; further annual reporting obligations apply under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act for registered foreign-invested companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a material-change or annual foreign-investment report can invalidate foreign investment recognition, remove FDI tax or regulatory advantages, and expose the company and foreign investor to administrative fines of up to KRW 10,000,000 as well as penalties under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, a Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily required to appoint an independent certified public accountant and obtain a statutory audit if: (a) total assets at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 12 billion; or (b) total assets equal or exceed KRW 7 billion but are below KRW 12 billion and the company also satisfies a secondary statutory trigger, including 100 or more regular employees, annual turnover at or above the regulatory revenue threshold, or consolidated-group reporting requirements; or (c) the company is a listed company, financial institution, or a parent required to present consolidated financial statements under K-IFRS. Headcount is not a standalone audit trigger, but it is a secondary quantitative factor in the asset-based threshold analysis. A company below all statutory triggers is not legally required to undergo an independent audit unless the articles of incorporation or a shareholder agreement imposes such an obligation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS as adopted by Korea for listed companies and for companies electing international standards; K-GAAP for non-listed Chusik Hoesa entities; Korean SME Accounting Standards for eligible smaller companies; all frameworks are interpreted in accordance with the Accounting Standards Board of Korea.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not currently operate a standalone public annual UBO filing for an ordinary domestic Chusik Hoesa; the controlling statutory rule is event-driven. Any share transfer, issuance, or redemption that changes ownership or beneficial ownership must be recorded immediately in the Register of Members and, for foreign shareholders, reported to MOTIE/KOTRA or the reporting foreign exchange bank within 30 days of the transaction. At the annual general meeting, the company must confirm the accuracy of the Register of Members and attached transfer records. Financial institutions also require refreshed beneficial-ownership information before activating or renewing banking, Stripe, cryptocurrency, or USDC-related payment arrangements in accordance with Korean AML CDD obligations.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 to USD 2,400 per annum for professional registered-office and corporate-secretarial support in Seoul or other major Korean business centers
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000 to USD 30,000 for a certified CPA statutory audit of a compliant Chusik Hoesa; USD 3,000 to USD 8,000 for an optional agreed-upon review or non-statutory assurance engagement when the company is below the mandatory audit threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal rate; progressive 9% up to KRW 200m, 19% up to KRW 20bn, 21% up to KRW 300bn, 24% above KRW 300bn
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-invested high-tech free-zone companies can obtain 100% corporate tax holiday for 3-5 years and 50% reduction for the next 2 years; R&D expenses for AI/LLM development qualify for incremental deductions of 20-40%, and foreign investment tax credits are available in Free Economic Zones.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return and Tax Base Calculation Form (Form 1) plus the Local Income Tax Surtax Return; filed electronically through National Tax Service HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before the last day of the month 3 months after the close of the fiscal year (March 31 for calendar-year entities); a one-month extension is available on request with guarantee, and up to 3 months if audited by a tax accountant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity name, corporate registration number, business place address, share code, and principal industrial classification (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541511).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the full name, country of residence, foreign tax ID, and shareholding percentage of each non-resident shareholder; if nominee or beneficial ownership exists, annex an anti-money-laundering beneficial owner declaration and a shareholder tax-residency certificate to avoid treaty misapplication on future dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income from Korean and foreign sources after statutory exclusions; foreign AI/LLM API token and license revenue must be included at gross revenue value.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Korean incorporated entities are tax-resident and taxed on global income. Any USDC or cryptocurrency proceeds received by offshore wallets from foreign customers must be converted to KRW at the NTS spot rate and reported here; failure to include foreign revenue gives rise to 40% fraudulent-filing surcharge and criminal liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory add-backs of expenses not deductible by law, including entertainment over ceilings, bribes, fines, and excessive payments to foreign related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments of royalties, management fees, or technical service fees to non-residents are deductible only if arm's-length and properly withheld; add back any amount paid to a low-tax jurisdiction or rejected for lack of economic substance, and reduce the tax base by reciprocal adjustments only if the corresponding transfer pricing documentation has been filed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit for foreign income taxes paid or withheld abroad, computed on a per-country basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the operative foreign tax certificate and prove that the foreign income was actually included in the Korean tax base. Non-resident recipients of dividends are not eligible; this line is for Korean-resident income, not for withholding on outbound distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of outbound dividends, interest, and royalties paid during the tax year, the applicable withholding tax rates and any treaty relief claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each non-resident dividend, royalty, or interest payment, show withheld 20% national plus 2% local income tax, or the treaty-reduced rate if the HomeTax non-resident withholding exemption application was approved before payment. Attach beneficial-owner substance evidence: corporate seats, decision-making minutes, transfer-pricing positions, business activity and unrelated third-party revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income inclusion for controlled foreign corporations held by Korean residents/shareholders in low-tax jurisdictions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If any non-resident shareholder controls a foreign subsidiary that processes AI-related IP or licensing, stratified CFC computations are required; the foreign corporation must not be excluded under the threshold of actual business activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing: negligent surcharge of 20% on the unpaid statutory tax; underreporting 10%; false or document-fraud 40% surcharge (Framework Act on National Taxes Art. 47-2/47-3). Daily interest accumulates at 0.022% for unpaid amounts. Criminal punishment for tax evasion or false reporting under Punishment of Tax Offenses Act can bring imprisonment up to 10 years and a fine up to 3 times the evaded tax, together with a travel ban and public blacklisting of the entity.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate withholding on gross outbound dividends (20% national corporate income tax plus 2% local income tax surtax).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before paying, file an electronically prepared application for tax exemption by treaty (NTS-prescribed Form 22 or equivalent) through HomeTax, attaching the shareholder's Tax Residency Certificate issued within 12 months, a beneficial ownership declaration, audited ownership information, and an economic substance statement. If the application is not approved, withhold at 22% and the non-resident may request a refund within 3 years after tax payment by filing an amended return. Treaty reductions in applicable DTAs are typically 5% to 15% for dividends, 0% to 10% for interest, and 0% to 10% for royalties depending on counterparty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory gross-basis withholding on non-resident royalties and intercompany interest payments is also 22% (20% national plus 2% local). Under applicable DTAs rates are generally between 5% and 15%; domestic thin-capitalization rules also apply to shareholders where debt-to-equity ratios exceed 3:1 for non-financial entities.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10,000,000,000 aggregate cross-border related-party transactions; Master File and Local File must be submitted to NTS within 9 months after the fiscal year-end, with an annual transfer pricing report attached to the corporate tax return.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No separate Economic Substance Regulations exist, but Korea applies the OECD BEPS beneficial-ownership and substance-over-form rule; a recipient of treaty-reduced withholding tax must exercise Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) functions—contract negotiation, pricing, AI-model development control, server capacity risk and credit management—in Korea, supported by payroll, office, board minutes and business records.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Corporate Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting AI/LLM inference API revenue credited from foreign clients to cryptocurrency wallets (USDC) and showing a loss in the Korean corporate return while actual crypto sales occurred through unbanked third-party processors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Offenses Act Art. 3: imprisonment up to 10 years and/or a fine up to 3 times the evaded taxes; under Framework Act on National Taxes Art. 47-3: 40% fraudulent-filing surcharge; criminal referral mandatory if the amount exceeds the tax criminal threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: On concealment or disclosure failure, the director is jointly liable for the unpaid corporate tax, interest, and penalties if the corporation lacks liquidity. The criminal court may impose a personal imprisonment sentence without corporate immunity; NTS can blacklist the company and the signing director, trigger travel-ban orders, seize personal foreign accounts, and require restitution of misappropriated proceeds before winding-up.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Noncompliance and Document Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling AI API compute capacity to an overseas related party below cost, or paying inflated royalties for open-source LLM algorithms, while failing to prepare or file the Local File, Master File and CbC report above the KRW 10 billion threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: International Tax Adjustment Act Art. 5: re-determination of taxable income and adjustment of the arm's length price; additional surcharge on income adjustment of 20%; deliberate documentation absence triggers a 40% fraud surcharge plus OCR penalties, and criminal prosecution for concealment if submitted transfer pricing documents are fabricated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the return and knowingly submit false transfer pricing documentation are treated as joint abettors; they can be ordered to compensate the firm and third-party shareholders under the Korean Civil Code Art. 750 (tort) and be disqualified from other board positions; travel restrictions and personal asset seizure are usually ordered to secure unpaid surcharges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / AML Beneficial Ownership Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Funneling Korean-source AI API licensing fees through a nominal foreign intermediary that has no office, no employees, and no bank account activity, while failing to disclose the true non-resident beneficiary to NTS, banks, or Korean investment counterparties, in order to claim treaty withholding tax relief fraudulently.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Foreign Investment Promotion Act and Specified Financial Information Act require full beneficial ownership reporting; false declarations supply fines up to KRW 100 million, deregistration of foreign investment status, and denial of all treaty relief. AML surveillance suspends payments and referrals to the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) trigger criminal sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The signer or substantial owner may be personally liable for false beneficial ownership statements: imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine of up to KRW 50 million under financial laws. The court may pierce the corporate veil and freeze personal assets, apply a travel ban (blacklisting), impose civil restitution to the tax state and third-party creditors, and order criminal imprisonment after conviction.
